+implementation("io.opentelemetry.instrumentation:opentelemetry-thrift-0.13:OPENTELEMETRY_VERSION")

+The instrumentation library provides the implementation of `ClientInterceptor` and `ServerInterceptor` to provide OpenTelemetry-based spans and context propagation.

+### Add the following dependencies to your project

+Replace `OPENTELEMETRY_VERSION` with the [latest release]( https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/io.opentelemetry.instrumentation/opentelemetry-grpc-1.6).

+implementation("io.opentelemetry.instrumentation:opentelemetry-thrift-0.13:OPENTELEMETRY_VERSION")

+
+The instrumentation library provides the implementation of `ClientInterceptor` and `ServerInterceptor` to provide OpenTelemetry-based spans and context propagation.

+// For server-side, decorate processor with a tracing wrapper.

[Testing] `AbstractThriftTest` already declares its own `AutoCleanupExtension` (used by all the `startServer` / `createClient` helpers). This duplicate field in the subclass is unused — please remove it (and the now-unused `AutoCleanupExtension` import).

[General] The advice's `typeMatcher`/`isMethod()` chain only matches methods whose **last** parameter is `AsyncMethodCallback`, so `args.length > 0` and the `instanceof` check are always true here — the wrapping can be unconditional. Also: `enterResult` from `inline = false` advice can be `null` only on early exit, but `methodEnter` always returns a 2-element array, so the `null` guard in `onExit` is dead too — consider removing it for clarity.

threads.body: The proxy invocation handler instruments every method call, including Object methods (toString/equals/hashCode). This can create unexpected spans for non-RPC calls; consider bypassing instrumentation when method.getDeclaringClass() == Object.class and directly invoking the underlying client.

replies.body: Fixed in 54f5a1300b — both client proxies now short-circuit `Object`-class methods.

threads.body: In the async client proxy, args can be null for no-arg/Object methods; accessing args.length will throw NPE. Also, Object methods should generally not be instrumented. Handle args == null (treat as empty array) and bypass instrumentation for Object.class methods to avoid NPEs and unintended spans.

replies.body: Fixed in 54f5a1300b — `Object`-class methods (which can pass `args = null` for zero-arg methods like `toString`/`hashCode`) are now short-circuited before the `args.length` check.

threads.body: endSpan() returns early when currentScope is null, but currentContext/currentRequest can be set earlier (when the context-propagation field is read) before readMessageEnd() creates the scope. If message parsing throws before readMessageEnd(), the started span will never be ended. Consider ending the span whenever currentContext/currentRequest are set (closing the scope only if non-null), or making the scope current immediately after instrumenter.start().

replies.body: Fixed in d4daa19be3 — `endSpan` now ends the span when `currentContext`/`currentRequest` are set, closing `currentScope` only if it was assigned.

threads.body: createAsyncClient() doesn't register cleanup for the TNonblockingTransport (and likely leaves the TAsyncClientManager selector thread running). This can leak sockets/threads across tests and cause flakiness. Defer cleanup for the transport and ensure the async client manager is properly closed/stopped if the API supports it.

replies.body: Fixed in 5605905f01 — registered `TNonblockingTransport` and `TAsyncClientManager.stop` with the cleanup extension.

threads.body: The "withCollision" test name suggests it validates a field-id collision with the context-propagation field, but the IDL uses field id 3333 while ContextPropagationUtil uses 8888. This test, ported from the OpenTracing test suite, ensures that methods whose argument struct uses the OT field id still work correctly with our `8888`. Keeping as-is.

threads.body: The method matcher instruments all methods except send_/recv_. This will also match Object methods (toString/equals/hashCode) and internal TServiceClient helpers like sendBase/receiveBase, which can lead to spans for non-RPC calls. Consider tightening the matcher (e.g., exclude Object methods and/or base helper methods) or explicitly short-circuiting in onEnter for Object.class methods.

replies.body: ByteBuddy's `applyAdviceToMethod` only visits methods declared on the matched type, not inherited ones. `sendBase`/`receiveBase` are declared on `TServiceClient` (which the type matcher excludes via `not(named(...))`), and `Object` methods are inherited so they aren't visited either. The remaining declared methods on the generated `*.Client` subclass are the RPC methods plus `send_`/`recv_` helpers that the name filter excludes. Keeping as-is.

threads.body: The README usage snippet doesn’t compile as written: `configureClient(CustomService.Client client)` / `configureClient(CustomService.AsyncClient asyncClient)` both reference an `openTelemetry` variable that isn’t in scope or passed as a parameter. Please update the example signatures (or show `openTelemetry` as an available variable) so users can copy/paste the snippet without errors.

The async client constructor advice binds `@Advice.Argument(2) TNonblockingTransport`, but the matcher only checks `takesArgument(0, TProtocolFactory)`. If Thrift adds another constructor whose first arg is a `TProtocolFactory` but doesn’t have argument 2, ByteBuddy can fail to apply this advice (disabling instrumentation). Consider tightening the matcher to the exact expected signature (e.g., takesArguments(3) + takesArgument(2, TNonblockingTransport)) and/or removing the unused `transport` binding.

replies.body: Fixed in fa3f3bc0020dc199c19234e3f9b21ee5e683eed5 — tightened the matcher with `takesArguments(3)` and `takesArgument(2, TNonblockingTransport)`, and dropped the unused `transport` advice binding.

Update: amended in 951e709125 — kept just the original `takesArgument(0, TProtocolFactory)` matcher and only removed the unused `@Advice.Argument(2) TNonblockingTransport` binding. `takesArguments(3)` would have over-tightened (Thrift's generator emits both 3-arg and 4-arg subclass ctors via `super(...)`, so both should be instrumented to wrap the protocol factory).

threads.body: `readFieldBegin()` treats any field with id `TRACE_CONTEXT_FIELD_ID` and type `MAP` as context propagation, regardless of which Thrift struct is currently being decoded. This means an application-defined nested struct that legitimately contains a `map<string,string>` field with id `8888` would have that field consumed and removed from the decoded data, causing a functional data loss/corruption bug. Consider scoping propagation detection to the top-level `*_args` struct for the current message (e.g., track struct nesting / current struct name) so only the dedicated propagation field is intercepted.

Injecting propagation in `writeFieldStop()` runs at the end of *every* struct serialization (including nested structs inside arguments). This makes it hard to guarantee the propagation field is written in a consistent/expected location (and forces the server-side reader to look for it in all nested structs, which increases collision risk with user fields). Consider injecting only when writing the RPC `*_args` struct (e.g., track the current struct name/depth from `writeMessageBegin`/`writeStructBegin`) so propagation is always attached to the request args wrapper.

threads.body: In `readMessageEnd()`, when the request doesn’t include the propagation field, socket lookup only uses `super.getTransport()`. For non-blocking servers, the socket/transport is often only available via `ServerCallContext` (as handled in `readFieldBegin()`), so network/server attributes can be missing for requests from non-instrumented clients. Consider applying the same fallback to `ServerCallContext.getTransport()` here too.

The builder stores/accepts AttributesExtractor with exact generic types. Other telemetry builders in this repo (e.g., GrpcTelemetryBuilder) use wildcards (e.g., `? super Request, ? super Response`) to make the API more flexible for user-defined extractors. Consider updating these lists and the add* methods to use `AttributesExtractor<? super ThriftRequest, ? super ThriftResponse>` to match existing public API patterns.
